name: Joseph
overview: Joseph was a male figure known as Joseph of Arimethea, noted in Matthew 27:57 as a member of the council, possibly the Sanhedrin, according to Luke 23:50. His identity is primarily marked by his unique attribute as a council member and his connection to Arimethea. No further tribal or familial details are provided in the given information.
namesAndTitles: The name Joseph, meaning 'he will add,' is a proper name mentioned in Matthew 27:56. This meaning reflects a hopeful or providential aspect but was not given directly by God in this instance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Joseph was a disciple of YHVH, explicitly stated in Matthew 27:57. Beyond this spiritual relationship, no additional family connections are documented in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Joseph of Arimethea holds significance as a faithful disciple who also held a position of authority within the Jewish council, indicating a respected status among his peers. His role in the gospel narrative connects him to the events surrounding Christ's passion, underscoring his faithfulness and courage. The prior summary of Joseph's life as the favored son of Jacob, who experienced suffering and exaltation, prefigures Christ’s own redemptive work, highlighting themes of providence and forgiveness central to God's plan.
